exposure: Place of labor onset (midwife-led care vs secondary care)
cohort: 223,739 women with a singleton pregnancy between 37 and 42 weeks gestation without a previous cesarean section, with spontaneous onset of labor and a child in cephalic presentation
finding: Starting labor in midwife-led care was associated with lower rates of severe acute maternal morbidity, postpartum hemorrhage, and manual removal of placenta compared to starting labor in secondary care, suggesting that midwife-led care at the onset of labor is safe for low-risk women in a well-structured maternity care system.
